tools.description: Search PutRoots' San Francisco rental index. Every row carries its source, the date we last saw it, and whether the landlord stated any requirements at all. tools.name: listing_requirements
tools.description: For one listing URL from search_listings: what the landlord requires, what the renter filled in, and the gap on each line — income, credit, SSN, deposit, pets, co-signer, documents. Each line carries the landlord's own sentence it was read from, plus where the rule came from and when we fetched it.

tools.description: The whole move at a glance for the signed-in person: days to move day, how many tasks there are, how many are settled, how many can be done right now, how many are blocked and how many are overdue, plus the critical path. Two rulers share that answer and they are not interchangeable: total and done

tools.description: The signed-in person's move events after an epoch-millisecond timestamp, oldest first — drafted, sent, called, answered, done, skipped. Use it to answer "what changed since we last spoke" without re-reading the whole plan. Capped; more says how many were left out.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "move_task_answer" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: listing_requirements · Private data: listing_requirements · Public sink: move_plan, move_task_draft.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: listing_requirements · Private data: listing_requirements · Public sink: move_plan, move_task_draft

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
